editorial:
Step into 1970s London where punk rock energy meets high fashion, and you follow Estella, a clever young grifter with big dreams and a wild streak. She teams up with two street thieves, and together they scrape by with charm, scams, and plenty of mischief. When her bold designs catch the eye of the Baroness, a cold and stylish fashion queen, Estella gets pulled into a glamorous world that is as dangerous as it is dazzling. The movie mixes heist fun, comedy, and a dark revenge story, so you get a lively ride with attitude, music, and eye-catching costumes.

Emma Stone and Emma Thompson are fantastic, bringing sharp energy and big personality to every scene. The costumes, soundtrack, and set pieces steal the show, while the pacing keeps things moving with twists and clever schemes. Some moments feel a bit long, and the story can get darker than expected, but the style and humor carry it well. If you enjoy fashion, revenge tales, or bold antiheroes, this is a fun pick.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Estella fully becomes Cruella and outsmarts the Baroness. She reveals the Baroness is her mother, then uses a clever plan to make the Baroness look guilty of murder while Cruella escapes with her friends. The Baroness is arrested, and Cruella takes over Hellman Hall, turning it into her new home. She also learns her real name and family history, setting up her future as the famous villain. It ends with Cruella confident, stylish, and ready for more trouble.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves bold fashion, clever revenge stories, and stylish antiheroes.
